c.tagline: China's futuristic tech boomtown by the sea.

taxi.color: Blue (electric BYD); red urban / green suburban zones

emergency.note: Fire is 119 and traffic police 122; English-speaking operators are hit-or-miss, so ask a local or hotel to call if possible.

hood_landmark.Futian: Ping An Finance Centre's Free Sky observation deck
hood_landmark.Luohu: Dongmen Pedestrian Street's massive shopping bazaar
hood_landmark.Nanshan: Shenzhen Bay Park's waterfront promenade and skyline views
hood_landmark.Bao'an: Fenghuang (Phoenix) Mountain's temple and hiking trails
hood_landmark.OCT (Overseas Chinese Town): Window of the World theme park's miniature global landmarks

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the crowded Dongmen/Luohu shopping areas and border crossings, and for counterfeit or bait-and-switch electronics scams around Huaqiangbei market.

hood_desc: Futian is Shenzhens central business and government district, home to the financial hub, upscale hotels and the Futian high-speed rail link to Hong Kong. It suits business travelers and first-time visitors who want a convenient, polished base.

Luohu is the older commercial core beside the Hong Kong border, packed with bustling markets like Dongmen and the Luohu Commercial City. It is livelier and more budget-friendly, ideal for shoppers and cross-border day-trippers.

Nanshan is the modern tech and coastal district, home to Tencent, top universities and the Shenzhen Bay waterfront with Sea World nightlife. It suits tech professionals, expats and families wanting a cleaner, greener setting.

Bao'an is the developing district surrounding the airport, more residential and industrial but increasingly modern with new malls and the coastal MixC. It is practical for travelers with early flights or airport connections.

OCT (Overseas Chinese Town) is a leafy leisure and culture zone with theme parks like Window of the World and Happy Valley plus the artsy OCT-LOFT creative quarter. It suits families and creative types seeking a relaxed, green atmosphere.

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or boiled water, which is the local norm even for residents.

transit.pay: Tap a rechargeable Shenzhen Tong card, or just scan a QR code in WeChat Pay/Alipay or the Metro app (no card needed, works for tourists with a foreign phone). Cards and top-ups are sold at station customer-service counters and vending machines. Fares start around ¥2 (~$0.30) and rise with distance, capped around ¥15 (~$2).
transit.hours: Trains run roughly 6:30am to 11pm-midnight depending on the line; there is no true overnight service.

food.name: Cantonese dim sum
food.desc: Hong Kong-style morning tea just over the border: har gow, siu mai, char siu bao and crispy shrimp dumplings with endless pots of tea.

places.name: Star of Canton
places.note: 20-plus-year institution; Trip.Best top local restaurant two years running for its crispy shrimp dumplings

places.name: Dragon Court
places.note: Praised in recent guides for refined Cantonese classics like shrimp dumplings with bamboo shoot tips

food.name: Chaoshan beef hotpot
food.desc: Ultra-fresh hand-cut beef, sliced by cut and swished seconds in clear broth, then dipped in sha cha sauce - a Chaoshan ritual Shenzhen has made its own.

places.name: Bahe Li Hai Ji (Baheli)
places.note: The famous Shantou-born chain; nearly every branch has queues for its hand-cut fresh beef

places.name: Chaofa Chaoshan Beef Hotpot
places.note: Beef arrives within 3 hours of butchering; a 2025 Trip.com local favorite, about 120-180 RMB pp

food.name: Chaoshan braised goose
food.desc: Lu e: goose slow-braised in a master soy-spice stock, sliced and served with garlic vinegar - the pride of Chaoshan kitchens across Shenzhen.

places.name: Chaoxiang Sihai
places.note: A polished introduction to Chaoshan-style braised goose per recent local guides

places.name: Roast Meat Street stalls
places.note: Gravy-drenched goose-leg rice at street prices, highlighted in 2025 local food press

food.name: Guangming roast pigeon
food.desc: Shenzhen's own delicacy: young squab from Guangming district farms roasted to crackling skin and juicy meat, eaten with the hands.

places.name: Guangming Guesthouse Restaurant
places.note: The historic home of the dish; locals drive out just for the pigeon

places.name: Star of Canton
places.note: Roast squab is a popular order alongside dim sum at this long-running Cantonese hall

food.name: Dongmen street snacks
food.desc: Beef offal stew, curry fish balls, grilled squid and sugar water desserts along Shenzhen's oldest market streets - eat where the queues are.

places.name: Dongmen Old Street
places.note: Shenzhen's most famous food street; dai pai dong stalls run late into the night

places.name: Huaqiangbei food alleys
places.note: Cheap, fast local eats tucked between the electronics markets

food.name: New-style cheese tea
food.desc: Fruit teas capped with whipped cheese foam - a Guangdong invention that conquered China, with two giant chains rooted in Shenzhen.

places.name: HEYTEA (flagship LAB stores)
places.note: The chain that popularized cheese tea; its big-city LAB flagships started in Shenzhen malls

places.name: Nayuki (Naixue de Cha)
places.note: Shenzhen-founded tea-and-bakery chain famous for fresh fruit cheese teas

food.name: Shenzhen craft beer
food.desc: A young city with a lively craft scene - hazy IPAs and lagers brewed by pioneers who started in urban-village garages.

places.name: Bionic Brew
places.note: Shenzhen's first craft brewery, founded 2014; still featured in 2025 local press

places.name: Peko Brewing Co.
places.note: Homegrown taproom that is a fixture of Shenzhen expat beer guides

landmarks: Ping An Finance Centre (Free Sky Observatory)
One of the world's tallest skyscrapers at 599 metres, its 116th-floor observation deck delivers dizzying views over Shenzhen's futuristic skyline.
Window of the World
Shenzhen's beloved theme park of 130 miniature world landmarks, from a 108-metre Eiffel Tower to pyramids, all in one photogenic afternoon.
Splendid China Folk Village
A twin park pairing miniature replicas of China's greatest monuments with full-scale ethnic villages showcasing dance, crafts and festivals of 56 nationalities.
Lianhuashan Park
A central hilltop park crowned by a bronze statue of Deng Xiaoping striding above the city he transformed from fishing village to megacity.
OCT-LOFT Creative Culture Park
A hip district of converted factories filled with galleries, indie cafés, design studios and weekend markets, the creative soul of Shenzhen.
Dafen Oil Painting Village
A famous urban village where thousands of painters once produced most of the world's replica canvases, now buzzing with original art and studios.
Shenzhen Bay Park
A 13-kilometre waterfront greenbelt of cycling paths and mangrove views across the bay to Hong Kong, glorious at sunset.
Wutong Mountain
Shenzhen's highest peak at 944 metres, a national scenic area of forest trails rewarding hikers with cloud-swept views over city and sea.
Dapeng Fortress
A remarkably preserved 600-year-old walled Ming garrison town on the eastern coast, its gates, temples and lanes recalling Shenzhen's pre-boom history.
Shenzhen Museum
A free flagship museum in the Civic Center district charting the city's meteoric rise alongside excellent folk-culture and ancient-history galleries.

intl.op: China Railway, Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed rail

train.note: High-speed trains from Futian and Shenzhen North run to Hong Kong West Kowloon in 15-30 minutes; although Hong Kong is part of China it is a full border crossing, so bring your passport and any needed permit and clear immigration at West Kowloon. Domestic high-speed trains from the same stations reach Guangzhou in about 30 minutes and cities nationwide - book on 12306 with ID. Futian is the more central station and is on the metro, while Shenzhen North handles the bulk of long-distance departures.

intl.to: Hong Kong (airport, Kowloon & Hong Kong Island)

bus.note: Cross-border coaches to Hong Kong leave from the Huanggang, Futian and Shenzhen Bay checkpoints; Trans-Island Chinalink, China Travel Service and Eternal East all run them, and Huanggang operates around the clock, which makes it the fallback when the trains and metro have stopped. A passport, and a mainland re-entry visa if you plan to come back, are required at the border. Domestic long-distance coaches use Luohu and Futian bus stations, but for anywhere on the high-speed network the train wins easily.

intl.to: Hong Kong (SkyPier at Hong Kong International Airport & the Hong Kong-Macau Ferry Terminal) - sails from Shekou Cruise Centre
Macau (Outer Harbour & Taipa) - sails from Shekou Cruise Centre

ferry.note: Cross-border ferries sail from the Shekou Cruise Centre in the west of the city, reachable on metro line 2. TurboJET's Shekou-SkyPier service lets air passengers transfer directly to flights at Hong Kong airport without clearing Hong Kong immigration, and boats also run to Macau in about an hour. Bring your passport, as these are full border crossings, and note that the airport sailings are timed to flight connections and must be booked with a matching air ticket. Services are cancelled outright when a typhoon signal 8 is hoisted.

half.name: Hong Kong
half.blurb: Just across the border, this dazzling city offers skyline views, harbor ferries, and endless shopping.

half.name: Guangzhou
half.blurb: The provincial capital draws visitors for its Cantonese food, riverside towers, and rich history.

half.name: Macau
half.blurb: This former Portuguese colony blends colonial ruins, ornate temples, and famous glittering casino resorts.

half.name: Zhuhai
half.blurb: A relaxed coastal city known for its breezy seaside promenade, islands, and gateway to Macau.

half.name: Dongguan
half.blurb: This neighboring manufacturing hub offers gardens, temples, and museums tracing the Opium War's history.

half.name: Foshan
half.blurb: Birthplace of famous martial artists, Foshan is known for its ancestral temple and Lingnan culture.
